note: DRAFT v1 module checks and final exam for the CARSI Hard Floor Care course. Original CARSI questions for Australian and New Zealand conditions; no IICRC standard text reproduced. Pass mark 80% for every check and the final exam (founder decision of 02/11/2026); the review pack's 90% final and must-pass questions are open founder decisions because the platform cannot enforce them. Answer positions balanced. SME review and sign-off required before seeding.

quizzes.title: CARSI Hard Floor Care — Module 1 check

questions.questionText: Which floor family does acid damage most?
questions.explanation: Acidic products can etch calcium-based stones such as marble and limestone, and etching changes the stone itself. The other floors have different weak points, and the maker's sheet decides their method.

questions.questionText: Why is steam a poor choice on coated timber?
questions.explanation: ATFA advises that steam cleaning is safest assumed unsuitable on timber unless the timber or finish maker approves it, because water and heat can get under the coating and into the boards.

questions.questionText: What is usually being cleaned on a hard floor?
questions.explanation: Most cleaning acts on the glaze, factory finish, polish or coating. Keeping that surface layer healthy is what keeps the floor lasting.

questions.questionText: A 1996 vinyl floor has no test results. What now?
questions.explanation: A floor laid before the ban that cannot be shown to be asbestos-free is treated as suspected asbestos-containing material. Stop and refer for competent assessment; do not try gentler work.

questions.questionText: When did the national asbestos ban start in Australia?
questions.explanation: The Australia-wide ban began on 31 December 2003. It did not remove asbestos already installed, which is why older floors need the asbestos question asked.

questions.questionText: In New Zealand, which buildings could contain asbestos?
questions.explanation: WorkSafe New Zealand says any building built or renovated before 2000 could contain asbestos. Newer parts of a building may be lower risk, but extensions and refurbishments before 2000 still count.

questions.questionText: Can you identify asbestos in a floor by sight?
questions.explanation: You cannot tell if materials contain asbestos just by looking. Colour, size and pattern do not clear a floor, so the decision rests on dates, records and competent assessment.

questions.questionText: Tiles are lifting on a floor that may hold asbestos. What do you do?
questions.explanation: Broken, lifting or crumbling tiles on a suspected asbestos floor are not a cleaning job. Stop, keep people away, and report it so competent people can assess it.

questions.questionText: What must be on site before a product is opened?
questions.explanation: Anyone who uses hazardous chemicals must keep copies of the SDS in the workplace. Read it before the product is opened, not after a problem.

questions.questionText: Which control should come first in the hierarchy?
questions.explanation: Safe Work Australia says to aim to eliminate risks first and ranks PPE among the least effective controls, so it never replaces controls higher in the order.

questions.questionText: What does AS 4586 classify?
questions.explanation: AS 4586 classifies the slip resistance of new pedestrian surface materials. A coating applied later can change how the floor grips, so record the class and any later test.

questions.questionText: What is the supply voltage for the machines you use?
questions.explanation: Australia and New Zealand supply is a nominal 230 V. The course examples use a 10 A outlet figure. Check each machine's data plate before plugging in.

questions.questionText: Two machines draw 5.5 A and 4.0 A. Using a 10 A outlet figure as the example, what is the total?
questions.explanation: Add the currents: 5.5 + 4.0 = 9.5 A, which leaves only 0.5 A of the 10 A example figure. On a real circuit, the machine currents plus everything else already on it must stay within the circuit's own rating, so confirm both before choosing: run one machine at a time or use a separate circuit with enough capacity.

questions.questionText: A new product arrives. Which step comes before the first use?
questions.explanation: The label and SDS state the dilution, hazards, protective equipment and surface warnings. Never mix two products, and never guess a dilution.

questions.questionText: You cannot identify the floor. What is the right step?
questions.explanation: If the floor or its coating cannot be identified, the limits of safe method cannot be set. Stop, test a hidden spot only as the maker allows, or ask the manufacturer.

questions.questionText: Which task is processing a crystalline silica substance under the Australian model WHS Regulations?
options: Raking out cement grout with a multi-tool
Applying sealer to granite with a roller
questions.explanation: Using a power tool to cut, grind or drill a material with at least 1% crystalline silica is processing. Cement grout can contain it, and a multi-tool is a power tool. The other tasks use no power tool on the material.

questions.questionText: In Australia, when may a respirator be the only control for silica processing?
options: Whenever the job is under one hour
When the worker has been fit-tested
Only when engineering controls are not reasonably practicable
When the material has less than 10% silica
questions.explanation: Controlled processing needs at least one engineering control, such as water or on-tool extraction, plus a respirator for remaining risk. A respirator alone is allowed only when those controls are not reasonably practicable.

questions.questionText: What is New Zealand's exposure standard for respirable crystalline silica?
questions.explanation: WorkSafe New Zealand lowered it to 0.025 mg/m³ (8-hour average) in November 2023. Australia's figure is 0.05 mg/m³, twice as high.

questions.questionText: Grinding is finished. How should the silica dust be cleaned up?
options: With an H-class vacuum or wet methods
With a broom, then a household vacuum
Left to settle overnight, then swept
questions.explanation: Dry sweeping, compressed air and general-purpose vacuums put the fine dust back in the air. Use wet methods or an H-class vacuum (Australia also allows M-class).

quizzes.title: CARSI Hard Floor Care — Module 2 check

questions.questionText: What comes before choosing a cleaning method?
questions.explanation: Naming the floor and its surface layer comes first, because the method depends on it. Five minutes of identification prevents most damage claims.

questions.questionText: A pale tile cannot be named. How do you treat it?
questions.explanation: If a stone cannot be identified, treat it as acid-sensitive, because a wrong guess on calcium-based stone etches it permanently. Use only products the maker states are safe for stone.

questions.questionText: Which record best identifies a floor?
questions.explanation: A maker's care sheet names the product and what suits it. Appearance and feel are starting points only.

questions.questionText: What do you do with a timber coating you cannot name?
questions.explanation: ATFA directs the reader to the coating manufacturer's advice. A coating you cannot name means the limits cannot be set, so stop.

questions.questionText: How big is a typical hidden-spot test?
questions.explanation: The test is small, out of sight and made with the intended product, dilution and dwell. The worked example uses 100 mm x 100 mm, which is 0.01 m2.

questions.questionText: What does the hidden-spot test record?
questions.explanation: The record ties the result to the exact product, dilution, dwell and floor. Without those details the test cannot be repeated or defended.

questions.questionText: What does a pH reading prove about a product?
questions.explanation: A pH reading is information about the solution. Surface compatibility, formulation, concentration and method also matter, so a reading never proves safety.

questions.questionText: What decides the dilution of a cleaner?
questions.explanation: The label states the dilution. One commercial vinyl maker's sheet says to always dilute chemicals to appropriate levels for each application.

questions.questionText: A label says 1 part product to 20 parts water. How much product is in 10 L of mix?
questions.explanation: One part in 21 is product: 10 divided by 21 is 0.476 L. Check the label's ratio each time, because 1:20 is only an illustration.

questions.questionText: Two products are both on the van. What is the rule?
questions.explanation: Never mix two products. Each SDS states incompatibilities, and a mix can release gas or damage the floor.

questions.questionText: Where do you find protective equipment for a product?
questions.explanation: The SDS states the hazards, the protective equipment, the first aid steps and spill steps. Keep a copy in the workplace.

questions.questionText: A cleaner's hidden-spot test dulls the gloss. What now?
questions.explanation: Any unexpected change or damage in gloss, colour or feel is a sign the product is incompatible with this floor. Stop, record it and obtain technical advice. Do not increase strength.

quizzes.title: CARSI Hard Floor Care — Module 3 check

questions.questionText: Which equipment suits rinse and recovery on grout?
questions.explanation: A truck-mount with a hard-surface spinner tool does rinse and recovery on tile, grout and rough stone. It needs separate truck-mount training and a plan for the wastewater.

questions.questionText: What sets a machine's working limits?
questions.explanation: The approved setup records the maker's values for this floor, coating, product and tool. Habit and last job's notes are how settings get copied wrongly.

questions.questionText: A maker says auto scrubbing takes about 20% of damp-mop time. What is the saving on a 2.0 h job?
questions.explanation: 20% of 2.0 h is 0.4 h, or 24 min. The saving is the other 1.6 h, which is 96 min. Time your own crew before quoting from one maker's ratio.

questions.questionText: Which area favours damp mopping over a scrubber?
questions.explanation: One maker's sheet says to use damp mopping in obstructed areas only and auto scrubbing in unobstructed areas.

questions.questionText: What must be true of a lead before use?
questions.explanation: Leads and plugs must be undamaged, with no cuts, taped joins or exposed conductors. Test-and-tag and the RCD test sit on top of that visual check.

questions.questionText: What is the first thing to do when a circuit trips mid-pass?
questions.explanation: A tripped circuit leaves a wet floor and a stopped machine. Make the area safe, find the cause such as total current or a damaged lead, and fix it before resuming.

questions.questionText: Which statement about pad colour is correct?
questions.explanation: Pads are specified by the maker for the product. There is no universal pad ladder that carries to every floor.

questions.questionText: A maker's sheet lists 300 rpm or lower for its own vinyl. What does that mean for other floors?
questions.explanation: That figure is an example of a maker specifying a setup for its own product. A different floor, coating or product has its own setup.

questions.questionText: Where does a pressure limit for a hard-surface tool come from?
questions.explanation: Pressure and temperature limits come from the makers of the floor, the grout and the tool, and are recorded in the approved setup.

questions.questionText: A limit cannot be found. What is the correct step?
questions.explanation: When a limit cannot be established, stop and obtain technical advice. Do not substitute a generic number or work upward from a guess.

questions.questionText: A 2 m2 test patch used 0.2 L. What rate does that give?
questions.explanation: 0.2 L over 2 m2 is 0.1 L per m2. Multiply by the floor area and add an allowance for edges and re-treatment.

questions.questionText: Why record where each setup value came from?
questions.explanation: A recorded source shows the value was taken from the maker, not guessed. That is the defence if a floor is later disputed.

quizzes.title: CARSI Hard Floor Care — Module 4 check

questions.questionText: What comes before any pressure on grout?
questions.explanation: Tap and scratch the grout in a grid first. Loose, crumbling or hollow results mean stop and quote remedial work, because the floor is not ready for a restorative clean.

questions.questionText: Grout crumbles at several test points. What do you quote?
questions.explanation: Crumbling grout means the floor cannot take a restorative clean. Quote remedial work or a re-grout instead of risking the grout and the owner's trust.

questions.questionText: What is done before wet work starts?
questions.explanation: Dry soil is vacuumed or dust-mopped first, as a maker's guide does before wet work. It stops slurry and protects the pads and brushes.

questions.questionText: Where must wastewater not go?
questions.explanation: NSW EPA guidance states that nothing other than clean rainwater should enter the stormwater drain. Confirm the trade-waste or council route first.

questions.questionText: An unknown stone is in a foyer. How is it treated?
questions.explanation: A stone that cannot be identified is treated as acid-sensitive until proven otherwise, because acid etching on calcium-based stone is permanent.

questions.questionText: What does AS 4586 classify?
questions.explanation: The standard classifies the wet slip resistance of a new surface. A coating applied later can change how the floor grips, so record the class and any later test.

questions.questionText: A coating is unknown. What is the step?
questions.explanation: Scratch a hidden area and put a water drop on it. Make a hidden-spot test with the intended product only as the maker allows. If the coating stays unknown or no approved test method is available, stop and obtain technical advice.

questions.questionText: Etched patches appear on a stone floor. What now?
questions.explanation: Etching changes the stone surface and is not a cleaning problem. A stone supplier advises seeking professional advice for dull or etched patches.

questions.questionText: When can grout sealer go on?
questions.explanation: The floor must be rinsed and fully dry first. A maker's guide says to remove rinse water and let the floor dry completely.

questions.questionText: A 300 mm tile is how many square metres?
questions.explanation: 0.3 m times 0.3 m is 0.09 m2. A 20 m2 floor holds about 222 tiles of that size.

quizzes.title: CARSI Hard Floor Care — Module 5 check

questions.questionText: A resilient floor has no records and is old. What first?
questions.explanation: A floor that cannot be ruled out as asbestos-containing is presumed, so the job stops and is referred. Looking at a floor cannot tell you.

questions.questionText: What must not happen to stripping solution?
questions.explanation: One maker's guide says not to allow stripping solution to dry on the floor. Dry residue is harder to remove and spoils the recoat.

questions.questionText: Which sheets set the method on a strip job?
questions.explanation: The floor, finish and stripper makers can each limit the method. The approved setup record names all three.

questions.questionText: What follows the strip and rinse?
questions.explanation: The floor must be rinsed, the rinse water removed and the floor fully dry. Verify residue removal by the finish maker's method before any coat.

questions.questionText: Where does strip wastewater go?
questions.explanation: Only clean rainwater goes to the stormwater drain. Confirm the site or council route before the first mix.

questions.questionText: What does ATFA advise about steam on timber?
questions.explanation: ATFA says that unless the floor or finish maker says it is OK, it is safest to assume steam cleaning is not appropriate on timber.

questions.questionText: How wet should a timber mop be?
questions.explanation: ATFA advises that the mop is wrung out until it is moist before mopping. Standing water is a hazard to boards and coating.

questions.questionText: A grey patch has worn through the coating. What next?
questions.explanation: Cleaning cannot restore worn coating. Photograph the patch with a scale, record it and refer it to a timber floor finisher.

questions.questionText: Which cleaner does ATFA name for damp mopping?
questions.explanation: ATFA advises a neutral pH wood floor cleaner or the product the finish maker recommends, and says to avoid harsh detergents and abrasives.

questions.questionText: 150 m2 at 10 m2 per litre needs how much mix?
questions.explanation: 150 divided by 10 is 15 L. The coverage figure is an illustration, so always use the label of the product on site.

quizzes.title: CARSI Hard Floor Care — Final exam

questions.questionText: An old floor cannot be ruled out as asbestos-containing. What do you do?
questions.explanation: A floor that cannot be ruled out is presumed to contain asbestos. The job stops and is referred, and no work method is taught or used.

questions.questionText: Who decides a floor is asbestos-free?
questions.explanation: A person cannot tell by looking. Only a written result from a competent person rules a floor out; otherwise it is presumed.

questions.questionText: Where do you find a product's hazards and first aid?
questions.explanation: The safety data sheet lists hazards, protective equipment and first aid. Keep a copy available at the workplace for the products you use.

questions.questionText: Why is no universal pH band taught?
questions.explanation: Limits come from the floor maker, the finish maker and the product label. A single band would be unsafe for some floors.

questions.questionText: What is the approved setup record for?
questions.explanation: The record names the floor, coating, product, dilution, dwell, tool and limits from the makers before the work starts.

questions.questionText: Limits cannot be established. What next?
questions.explanation: If a limit cannot be established from the makers' sheets, stop and obtain technical advice. A guess or a copied setting is not an approval.

questions.questionText: What is checked on a machine before use?
questions.explanation: The pre-start check covers leads, plug, RCD, guards and the pad or brush. A damaged lead or a failed RCD means the machine does not run.

questions.questionText: Which supply figures do the course power examples use?
questions.explanation: The examples use 230 V and a 10 A outlet figure. The circuit's own rating is confirmed on site, and a machine and its leads must suit it.

questions.questionText: Grout is loose at several test points. What next?
questions.explanation: Loose or crumbling grout means the floor cannot take a restorative clean. Quote remedial work or a re-grout and use no pressure.

questions.questionText: Which stone is sensitive to acidic products?
questions.explanation: Calcium-based stones such as marble and limestone are etched by acidic products, and etching is permanent.

questions.questionText: What must stripping solution never do on the floor?
questions.explanation: One maker's guide says not to allow stripping solution to dry on the floor. Dried residue is harder to remove and spoils the recoat.

questions.questionText: A steam mop is offered for a timber floor. What is safest?
questions.explanation: ATFA advises that unless the floor or finish maker says it is OK, it is safest to assume steam cleaning is not appropriate on timber.

questions.questionText: A grey patch has worn through the coating. What next?
questions.explanation: Cleaning cannot restore worn coating. Photograph the patch with a scale, record it and refer it to a timber floor finisher.

questions.questionText: 120 m2 at A$14 per m2 gives what before GST?
questions.explanation: 120 times 14 is 1,680. Adding 10% GST gives 1,848. The rate is an illustrative example, not a market rate.

questions.questionText: A$1,680 plus 10% GST totals what?
questions.explanation: 10% of 1,680 is 168, so the total is 1,848. Confirm the GST rate that applies in your country.

questions.questionText: What goes on the handover page?
questions.explanation: The handover page holds the floor, setup lines, photos, the maker's return-to-use time, the care sheet and the next service date.

questions.questionText: Where does tile cleaning wastewater go?
questions.explanation: NSW EPA guidance states that nothing other than clean rainwater should enter the stormwater drain. Use the approved site or council route.

questions.questionText: What does AS 4586 set out?
questions.explanation: The standard classifies the wet slip resistance of new pedestrian surfaces. A later coating can change how the floor grips.

questions.questionText: Who records Met or Not yet on the practical day?
questions.explanation: An assessor watches each task and records Met or Not yet against the criteria. Critical criteria must all be met.

questions.questionText: Which unit does this course use for area?
questions.explanation: The course uses metric units first, so areas are in square metres. Machine power examples use 230 V and a 10 A outlet figure.
